item.title: Why I still draft in the age of AI: A practical guide to writing with LLMs
item.description:
When ChatGPT was released in 2022, my employers encouraged me to use it for writing, but no one explained how to use it, let alone how not to.

Like many people, I started by using it to generate first drafts. I’d read through the first draft and realize I didn’t agree with half the arguments. By the time I’d corrected the reasoning and rewritten the paragraphs, I could’ve written the whole thing myself. There was something else that bothered me. If I let AI develop my arguments, was I really doing the intellectual work of writing?

item.title: Jupiter Lend Under Stress: Analyzing the October 10 Liquidation Event
item.description:
On October 10, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. would impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports. This announcement was followed by a rapid market selloff: over the course of October 10, the price of ETH fell as much as 12% and SOL fell as much as 24%.

The wave of selling ultimately triggered $19B in liquidations across derivative markets. But how did this affect other venues that offer leverage, like credit markets?

item.title: The DeFi Lending Endgame
item.description:
Lending is one of the oldest functions in finance. A lender lets a borrower turn $1 of collateral into more than $1 worth of financial exposure while charging interest for it. Homeowners do this with a home equity line of credit (HELOC), and options traders do this with margin. The modern economy relies on credit for various financial functions demonstrating a clear product-market fit.

Crypto performs the same function through lending protocols. A user deposits an asset, borrows against it, and pays interest on the loan. Aave, the leading lending venue, accepts USDC, EUR, and gold-pegged assets as collateral and intermediates ~$10B in active loans. The base primitive supports cash-and-carry trades and long and short positions, and it has grown into curated vault products through protocols like Morpho which recently integrated with Coinbase. In structure these venues now resemble global FX markets.

item.title: Building an Agentic Pipeline for Onchain Data Analysis
item.description:
Using an LLM for data analysis can sometimes create more problems than it solves. In a chat-based workflow, the analyst still has to supply table schemas, API documentation, and project-specific context while copying and pasting data between multiple interfaces and tools. If you’re not careful, this setup can increase token costs and introduce errors – undermining the time saved by using an LLM in the first place.

At Blocmates, we created an agentic pipeline to automate these tasks. Instead of manually providing context and coordinating each step, the analyst fills out a data specification and sends it to Claude Code. The agent loads the necessary context, writes SQL queries, fetches data from APIs, and tests and publishes the queries to Dune.

item.title: Building a Local AI System for Financial Markets & Digital Asset Intelligence
item.description:
Financial markets generate an enormous amount of information every day, from macroeconomic developments to digital asset markets and protocol governance. In the past, I’ve struggled to keep up with these developments while writing research reports.

So to streamline my research process, I built a locally hosted AI system that aggregates news and market data, identifies important developments, and generates daily research briefings. Using locally hosted language models, the system has reduced my daily news intake from 1–2 hours to approximately 20 minutes.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 2
item.description:
In Part 1, we identified Jupiter Lend’s liquidation instructions, mapped their account arguments, and decoded the raw amounts of debt repaid and collateral seized.

In this walkthrough, we’ll combine those findings into a single DuneSQL query using common table expressions (CTEs). The query reconstructs liquidation records from raw instructions and joins Dune’s prices.hour table to calculate the USD value of debt repaid and collateral seized.

We’ll work through the query in four phases, following how each CTE transforms and passes data to the next. Select a CTE in the interactive query below to explore its role in building the final dataset.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 1
item.description:
Most onchain analysis starts with the assumption that someone has already decoded the dataset. On platforms like Dune, analysts can usually query human-readable tables without having to interpret the raw bytes recorded onchain.

But what if the dataset you need doesn’t exist?

I ran into this problem while trying to analyze liquidations on Jupiter Lend during the market selloff on October 10, 2025. I wanted to determine how many liquidations were processed and their total value.

item.title: About
item.description:
I’m Malachi (Kai) Dofat. I’m a liberal arts graduate who got increasingly technical.

I studied English and began my career as an editorial assistant at Increment, Stripe’s quarterly magazine for software development teams.

Over the past four years, I’ve expanded beyond writing into technical research, data analysis (SQL & Python), and software implementation. Now, I write about technology and build tools and workflows that solve practical problems.

Much of my work has focused on financial software and blockchain infrastructure, but my interests extend to AI, data workflows, and building tools that make research and everyday work easier.
